description:
Four independent robustness gaps in the plan-capture subsystem, each a separate
failure mode from the missing CI gate (tracked in plan-capture-blocking-ci-gate):

1. Implicit phase-eligibility. adapter.py:120 defaults
   plan_capture_phase_eligible=True and ~12 SaaS adapters inherit it implicitly.
   It is a correctness-critical flag (it decides whether plan capture is isolated
   from measured timing); a future non-EXPLAIN subclass would silently inherit
   True.
2. Timeout thread leak. On a capture timeout, result_capture.py:828 leaves a live
   EXPLAIN thread on the measurement connection (an accepted tradeoff). It cannot
   perturb MEASURED timing (post-measurement phase), but it can corrupt SUBSEQUENT
   captures in the same phase - untested.
3. Plan identity / misattribution. Plans are captured and attached by query_id,
   but for stream/seed-specific SQL (TPC power-test streams, unseeded variants)
   the SQL bound to a query_id can differ from the measured statement, so the
   attached plan may describe a different query text than the one timed.
4. Comparable-subset honesty. The cross-engine comparable subset is an
   operator-type multiset over a single query shape (test_cross_engine_
   conformance.py) with no tables/predicates - a meaningful harmonization check but
   near-trivial as "plan equivalence". Either strengthen it or relabel it so
   consumers do not over-trust it.

anti_patterns.dont: claim cross-engine plan equivalence from an operator-type multiset
make plan-capture eligibility a silent base default for new adapters

preserves.behavior: The centralized is_dml_query double-execution guard is unchanged.
The post-measurement capture phase stays isolated; measured timing is unaffected by any change here.

verifications.description: No adapter relies on the implicit eligibility default
verifications.expected: passes; every concrete adapter declares plan_capture_phase_eligible in its own class dict

verifications.description: Per-result plan identity holds across same-id streams
verifications.expected: each result's plan matches its executed_sql; two same-query_id streams carry distinct plans

work_units.notes:
Declare plan_capture_phase_eligible explicitly on every concrete adapter
(matching DuckDB/PG/Redshift). Add a unit test asserting no adapter relies on
the inherited base default for this flag (introspect the class dict, not the
resolved attribute).
work_units.summary: Make plan_capture_phase_eligible explicit on every adapter and assert no implicit inheritance

work_units.notes:
Add a test reproducing back-to-back captures where the first times out, then
either fence the measurement connection (reset/reconnect before the next
capture) or serialize captures behind a fresh connection. Preserve the
post-measurement isolation guarantee (measured timing unaffected).
work_units.summary: Bound the capture timeout thread so it cannot corrupt subsequent captures

work_units.notes:
Audit _capture_plans_post_measurement / _merge_plan_capture_into_result so each
result carries the plan of ITS executed_sql. Add a test with two streams of the
same query_id whose SQL differs, asserting each result carries its own plan
(no cross-stream misattribution).
work_units.summary: Key plan capture/attachment on the result's exact executed SQL, not query_id alone

work_units.notes:
Either add table-identity to the comparable subset and expand the conformance
corpus to >=3 query shapes, OR relabel it in docs/output as "operator-shape
harmonization" (not plan equivalence) so consumers do not over-trust matching
subsets. Recommend the relabel unless multi-engine plan comparison becomes a
published feature. Pick one and record the decision.
work_units.summary: Strengthen or honestly relabel the cross-engine comparable subset
